text:
elaine_cs: FYI Moorland (acct: moorland-prod) pinging support — they've seen p99 for text-generation spike from ~1200ms to 6s since ~11:30 PST and it's impacting UI. They attached a curl example and said retries aren't helping.

miguel_oncall: Thanks Elaine — can you paste their sample request + tenant id? I'm going to check queue depth and our per-tenant throttles.

elaine_cs: Tenant ID: tenant_moorland_01. Sample request they sent:
```bash
curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -d '{"model":"open-lama-3b","input":"summarize: long doc...","max_tokens":512}'
```

sam_sre: I pulled the last 2h from traces. p95 is ~1.3s but p99 jumps to 5-7s for Moorland specifically. Other tenants on same pool look fine. Queue depth for tenant_moorland_01 peaked at 18 (our usual is <3). There are periodic spikes of concurrent long-running requests from a few client IPs.

sam_sre: Snippet from runtime logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-12T18:28:47Z pool=us-west-2a pool_id=gpu-pool-3 tenant=tenant_moorland_01 request_id=abc123 state=queued queue_pos=14
2026-03-12T18:28:49Z pool=us-west-2a instance=gpu-07 tenant=tenant_moorland_01 state=running seq_len=1024 est_exec_ms=4200
2026-03-12T18:28:53Z pool=us-west-2a instance=gpu-07 tenant=tenant_moorland_01 state=running seq_len=1024 kv_hits=0
2026-03-12T18:28:56Z pool=us-west-2a instance=gpu-07 tenant=tenant_moorland_01 state=complete latency_ms=5860
```

tara_eng: Looks like long sequence lengths (1k tokens) + no KV caching used. Moorland recently enabled a bulk-batch feature in their client last week — could be sending many large requests concurrently. Any noisy neighbor detection showing one actor?

sam_sre: Yes — traffic fingerprinting shows ~4 distinct source IPs for tenant_moorland_01 that dominate 70% of their long requests. The load pattern is bursty: 40 requests x large seq within a couple minutes. The scheduler doesn't preempt short jobs so the long jobs push short ones to queue => p99 skew.

miguel_oncall: Two mitigation options: 1) per-tenant reservation (short-term) or 2) create an allowlist to route Moorland traffic to a burst pool or dedicated warm slot. We can also apply soft rate limits for the offending IPs if they consent. Elaine, did they ask for any specific mitigation?

elaine_cs: Moorland asked for a \"fast fix\". They suggested we add their service IP range (54.23.0.0/16 and 3.120.44.0/24) to some priority path if possible. They prefer avoid throttling because it impacts other services.

sam_sre: I can do a temporary routing rule to send their IPs to a reserved burst pool (if capacity exists) or to a lower-latency lane. That would reduce p99 but might cost them more tokens — need billing note.

tara_eng: Also can enable prefix/KV caching for their workload if they use repeated prompts. But if sequences vary, caching won't help. We should run a quick eval of repetition in their payloads.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: create-routing-rule(routing: priority-route-moorland, src_cidrs=[54.23.0.0/16,3.120.44.0/24], target_pool=gpu-burst-1, ttl=6h) by sam_sre — awaiting approval.

miguel_oncall: I give 👍 to route for 6h as a mitigator. Elaine, get Moorland to confirm the exact CIDRs and confirm billing tradeoff. I'll also enable tenant-level observability alerts.

elaine_cs: Confirmed — they approve the two CIDRs and understand potential cost. They've asked for an allowlist/priority route for the next 6 hours and then to meet for long-term solution.

sam_sre: Rolling the route now. Command I ran (internal):
```bash
redwoodctl routing create --name priority-route-moorland \
  --src-cidrs 54.23.0.0/16,3.120.44.0/24 \
  --target-pool gpu-burst-1 \
  --ttl 6h \
  --notes \"temp mitigate tenant_moorland_01 p99 spike\"
```

ops-bot: routing-change: priority-route-moorland created by sam_sre at 2026-03-12T18:43:12Z (id=rout-9921).

sam_sre: After creating route: immediate drop in queue depth for tenant_moorland_01 from 18 -> 2. p99 back to ~1.4s within two minutes. Monitoring for recurrence.

tara_eng: I'll open an engineering ticket to evaluate three items: 1) auto-detect bursty large-sequence tenants and offer automated reservations, 2) add soft preemption for long-running jobs in mixed-tenant pools, 3) surface client-side best-practices (batching, token budgets).

miguel_oncall: Also we should consider adding an allowlist workflow in Console so CS can onboard priority routes without infra intervention. Elaine please file a support request template to collect CIDRs, billing approval, desired duration — we'll use that for future.

elaine_cs: Filed SUPPORT-4872 with the Moorland confirmation, CIDRs, and billing ack. Added note: \"customer requests post-mitigation meeting to discuss dedicated reservation and SDK changes.\"

tara_eng: Engineering owner: tara_eng. Ticket: INF-3219. ETA to triage: 48h.

sam_sre: Post-mortem notes so far: root cause = tenant-origin bursty long-sequence requests causing queue contention on shared GPU pool; short-term fix = priority routing for CIDRs; medium-term = reservation/auto-detect/preemption features.

miguel_oncall: I'll follow up with Moorland at EOD with the mitigation summary and a link to the observability dashboard. Closing loop once the 6h TTL expires or earlier if they ask.

elaine_cs: Moorland replied: \"Thanks, saw immediate improvement. We'll schedule a meeting tomorrow to discuss reserved capacity.\" :white_check_mark:

sam_sre: Leaving a note to revert route at TTL expiry. Also will add a scheduled check in 2h to ensure no bleed-through.

ops-bot: scheduled-task: check-tenant-queue-depth (tenant_moorland_01) at 2026-03-12T20:43:12Z.

miguel_oncall: Good job team — short outage avoided. Action items: Elaine -> customer follow-up & billing ack (done), Tara -> INF-3219 triage, Sam -> monitor + revert route if stable.

elaine_cs: Thanks all. I'll update SUPPORT-4872 with the meeting time and attach the sample traces.

sam_sre: Adding final log extract for records:
```
before: p99=6300ms qdepth=18
after: p99=1400ms qdepth=2 (priority-route active)
```

tara_eng: We'll discuss longer term on INF-3219. Closing thread unless anyone sees regressions. :eyes:
